title: reconcile-apply's ok predicate compares id-blind sums, so a surplus can mask a shortfall
description:
From TASK-199's gating review (MEDIUM). **Pre-existing — not introduced by TASK-199**, which correctly scoped itself to replace-bucket visibility. The same masking existed with installs alone from the TASK-181/183 era.

**The defect.** `bin/pack-ctl.js:470-478` compares **combined totals**: `plannedInstallCount + plannedReplaceCount` against `installedCount + replacedCount`. Because the comparison is id-blind, a surplus landing in one place numerically offsets a genuine shortfall elsewhere, and the run reports `ok: true`.

**Surpluses are real, not hypothetical.** Per-pack `reconcilePack` re-plans against only *that pack's* desired set, so a per-pack plan can diverge from the aggregate `computedPlan` the predicate was built from.

**Concrete scenario, reachable with today's built-ins** (the reviewer's): the lock holds `skill:watch` with `owners: []` (orphaned) while the watch pack still desires it and it is live on disk. Design-power's per-pack plan — which does not desire `watch` — removes it; the watch pack then reinstalls it. That is a **landed install that was never in the aggregate plan**. If design-power's planned `ui-ux-pro-max` install soft-fails in the same run: planned = 1, landed = 1, `ok: true` — and the failure is invisible except in the nested `packs[].report`.

**Why this matters more than the arithmetic.** `commands/design-pack.md` Step 4 and the module header both state the stronger **per-bucket** semantics — `installed_count === planned_install_count` AND `replaced_count === planned_replace_count`. The sum comparison only implements that when per-pack plans partition the aggregate exactly. So the documented contract is not the implemented one: a doc-vs-code gap on the very predicate that exists to make failures visible.

This is the Empty-result contract's own subject matter — an operation reporting unqualified success for an ambiguous case — appearing in the mechanism built to prevent it.

**Suggested fix (the reviewer's).** Make the comparison identity-aware: track planned op ids per bucket and compare against landed op ids per bucket, rather than counting. That closes the offset class and makes the documented semantics literally true. Keep the existing `failureKind` precedence (`aborted` > `total` > `partial`) and the `E_PACK_APPLY_<KIND>_FAILURE` code namespace — one convention, extended, not a second one.

**Do not regress what TASK-199 established:** deferred replaces (installed-newer, or undecidable non-semver divergence) must stay excluded from "planned", or a correct keep-as-is run starts reporting `ok: false`. TASK-199's mutation plants pin that behaviour; re-run them.
acceptance_criteria: A failing spec first reproduces the masking: a run where a landed-but-unplanned op offsets a genuinely soft-failed planned op reports ok:true today. Capture the red-run output verbatim.
The comparison is identity-aware per bucket - planned op ids versus landed op ids - so a surplus in one bucket can no longer offset a shortfall in another.

The documented semantics in commands/design-pack.md Step 4 and bin/pack-ctl.js's module header are literally true of the implementation after the change; if any gap remains, it is stated rather than implied.

Deferred replaces stay excluded from planned: re-run TASK-199's mutation plants (totals blinded to replace terms; shippedPinWins filter dropped; replacedCount hardcoded) and confirm all three still fail.
failureKind precedence and the E_PACK_APPLY_<KIND>_FAILURE code namespace are unchanged - one convention extended, not a second introduced.
The design-pack doc-lock still derives its checked set from real success AND failure runs, and still fails if a documented field is removed from the doc.
npm run test:all is green; dist/pack-ctl.cjs rebuilt and committed, with dist-parity passing.

comments.author: reviewer
comments.body:
**APPROVE** — final verdict. FULL depth, tier `tdd`. **0 HIGH / 1 MEDIUM (process, discharged) / 4 LOW, two of them closed in a follow-up round.**

Commits: `4f00181` (fix + tests), `d923e18` (id-boundary hardening + message fix), `47961c8` (dist rebuild).

## Gate

`test:since -- ba85192` 12 files / 160 passed, no zero-selection marker ⬛ `npm test` 89 files / 1186 passed, 2 skipped ⬛ `test:all` **191 passed | 1 skipped (192 files), 2222 passed | 4 skipped, 0 failed** (Orchestrator-verified independently on a quiesced tree, identical numbers) ⬛ named e2e 4 files / 38 passed including all-8-bundle dist-parity ⬛ `check:calibration` clean.

## Round 1 — independently reproduced, not taken on trust

**Red run (AC1):** the pre-fix `computeApplyOutcome` was extracted from `ba85192` into a scratchpad with real `src/pack-apply.js` predicates and all six new tests' assertions replayed: **6 failed / 6**. The two load-bearing ones are genuine — T1 fails `ok: expected true to be false` with the two assertions *before* it passing, so `installedCount === 1 === plannedInstallCount` really is the numeric coincidence that hid the soft-failed `skill:ui-ux-pro-max`.

**Mutation plants (AC4) — all three re-run, counts matching exactly.** Plant A (identity totals blinded to replace terms) → 4 failed; **Plant B (`shippedPinWins` dropped) → 1 failed, and the right one** (`T199-3 DEFERRED replace is NOT planned and stays ok:true — plannedReplaceCount: expected 1 to be 0`); Plant C (`replacedCount` hardcoded 0) → 2 failed; unmutated control → 0. The deferred-replace exclusion is genuinely pinned.

**Adversarial sweep — 18 old-vs-new cases.** Every `ok:true → ok:false` flip is a real defect being caught (same-bucket surplus, cross-bucket surplus, duplicate-id masking, wrong-bucket landing). Every case that must stay green does (empty plan, surplus-with-nothing-planned, deferred installed-newer, deferred non-semver git-sha). Over-correction was also chased **structurally**: for a planned install id to be absent from `landedInstallIds` while the op succeeded, the skill would have to become live by something other than an install op, and `src/pack-reconcile.js:207` makes install the only materializer for a not-live skill — so the wrong-bucket false alarm is unreachable.

**AC6 doc-lock did not regress** — untouched since `e6a9810` (TASK-184), still running both a success fixture and a forced-failure fixture, still word-boundary matching. Critically, `missingInstallIds`/`missingReplaceIds` are consumed only by the `message` template and **not** spread into the returned payload, so `Object.keys(result)` is unchanged and the documented output shape is untouched.

**AC3** — both doc sites literally true, and explicit rather than glossing: *"which makes the raw sums legitimately NOT equal `planned_install_count`/`planned_replace_count` even on a fully successful run — do not treat `installed_count === planned_install_count` as the success test."* A repo-wide sweep found no third stale site.

## Follow-up round — both LOWs closed at the right level

**The conditional fail-closed claim — hardened, not softened.** Landed-id `Set`s now keep string ids only; the missing-check short-circuits any non-string planned id before the `Set` lookup. **The asymmetry is what makes it work:** the filter applies only to the *landed* sets, never the planned ones, so a malformed planned id stays counted in `plannedIdentityTotal`, lands in `missingInstallIds`, and is subtracted from `matchedIdentityTotal` — nothing is dropped from either side. Verified across seven probes: the original counter-example (`install: [{}]`, `installed: [undefined]`) now gives `ok=false, kind='total'`; planned `42` vs landed `'42'` stays missing (the `typeof` guard fires before the lookup, so no coercion path can satisfy it); a landed array polluted with `[null, undefined, 7]` cannot manufacture a match.

**The empty render — provably unambiguous.** The reachable state space was brute-forced (3×4×3×4×2 = **288 combinations**): `ok:false` with both buckets rendering `[none]` occurs in 49 combos, and **in 0 of them is the abort clause absent**. `failureKind` can only be non-null with zero missing ids via the `anyAborted` branch, so the one shape that could read as "it failed but nothing is missing" always ships its own explanation in the same string. `(missing id)` keeps the malformed case visually distinct. **This is the Empty-result contract satisfied inside the ticket's own output, which is the right place for it.**

**Bundle delta audited:** `47961c8` is 9 insertions / 5 deletions across exactly four hunks, each mapping 1:1 to a source change. No unrelated churn, no esbuild drift. Also confirmed TASK-207's later re-stale/re-rebuild of the same bundle did not clobber it — HEAD still carries `formatMissingIds` and the four `typeof id === "string"` guards, with zero remaining bare `.join` sites.

## The second bug this fix closes

The developer classified its duplicate-id test failure as weak evidence. It was not — the pre-fix predicate genuinely **false-alarmed** (`ok:false, partial`) whenever two packs desired the same not-yet-live skill, reachable because `aggregateDesired` concatenates `resolveDesired` across packs with no dedup and `plan()` pushes one install op per desiring pack. **The fix is strictly better in both directions**: it closes the masking class *and* removes a pre-existing false alarm. Now documented on the test that covers it.

## Concurrency handling — noted approvingly, no finding

Faced with 2 failures from another agent's live edits, the developer stashed only the unrelated dirty paths, verified its bundle byte-matched a clean-tree build, then stash-popped to restore the other agent's work — rather than committing dist from a contaminated tree or chasing another ticket's red. Holding the rebuild out of `d923e18` into a separate `47961c8` is what made the delta auditable in one glance.

## Carry-forward (not a blocker)

Identical non-string planned ids collapse to one `Set` entry, so `missingInstallIds` under-counts malformed ops while `ok` stays correctly `false` — it under-counts the diagnostic, never under-reports the failure. Same `Set`-collapse the JSDoc already documents for duplicate ids.

**Verdict: APPROVE.**

comments.body:
**CLOSED on a green independent review.** Review depth **FULL**; rubric inputs: the diff touches packaging/dist (`dist/pack-ctl.cjs`) and the `reconcile-apply` success/failure predicate itself — the mechanism whose whole job is making failures visible. Packaging alone forces FULL; round 1 was also 288 changed lines (288+/51-) across 4 files.

Commits `4f00181` (fix + tests), `d923e18` (id-boundary hardening + message fix), `47961c8` (dist rebuild). **The commit graph is interleaved with TASK-204 and TASK-207**, so this ticket's diff is non-contiguous.

## What was fixed

`bin/pack-ctl.js` compared **combined totals** — `plannedInstallCount + plannedReplaceCount` vs `installedCount + replacedCount`. Being id-blind, a surplus in one bucket numerically offset a genuine shortfall in another and the run reported `ok: true`. Pre-existing, not introduced by TASK-199. Surpluses are real: per-pack `reconcilePack` re-plans against only that pack's desired set, so a per-pack plan can diverge from the aggregate plan the predicate was built from.

The comparison is now identity-aware per bucket — planned op ids vs landed op ids as `Set`s — keeping the existing `failureKind` precedence (`aborted > total > partial > null`) and the `E_PACK_APPLY_<KIND>_FAILURE` namespace byte-identical. One convention extended, not a second introduced.

## The fix turned out to be strictly better in BOTH directions

The developer's own red run contained the evidence and it **under-classified it** — calling the duplicate-id failure weak "field didn't exist yet" evidence when it was a real `ok: expected false to be true`. The reviewer's replay caught that.

It documents **a second, pre-existing bug this fix closes as a side effect**: the old predicate **false-alarmed** (`ok:false, partial`) whenever two packs desired the same not-yet-live skill — genuinely reachable, because `aggregateDesired` concatenates `resolveDesired` across packs with no dedup and `plan()` pushes one install op per desiring pack. So the change closes the masking class *and* removes a false alarm. Neither the commit message nor any AC named it; it is recorded here and on the test that covers it. **Erring by under-claiming your own evidence is the right direction to err**, and I would rather have that than the reverse.

## Two LOWs were worth a follow-up round, and both landed at the right level

1. **The fail-closed claim was conditional while the JSDoc stated it absolutely.** It rested on `src/pack-reconcile.js:192` building ids as `` `skill:${resource.id}` `` — an invariant owned by another module and pinned by no test. The reviewer proved the claim breaks when it does: `computedPlan.install: [{}]` with `packs[0].installed: [undefined]` returned **`ok: true`**, fail-**open**. **I asked for hardening rather than softening the wording**, and that was the right call — the guarantee is now enforced at the boundary this module owns. The asymmetry is what makes it correct: the string filter applies only to the *landed* sets, never the planned ones, so a malformed planned id stays counted as planned, lands in `missingInstallIds`, and is subtracted from matched. Nothing is dropped from either side. This was the **third** absolute-doc-claim-over-conditional-behaviour finding this batch (TASK-197 and TASK-198 each had one).

2. **`[undefined].join(', ')` rendered `missing planned installs: []` on an `ok:false` run** — an empty list as the explanation for a failure, which is the exact "absence reads as evidence of absence" shape this ticket exists to close, appearing in this ticket's own operator-facing output. Now `none` for a genuinely empty bucket and `(missing id)` for a malformed entry. The reviewer brute-forced the reachable state space (**288 combinations**) and proved it unambiguous: `ok:false` with both buckets rendering `[none]` occurs in 49 combos and **in zero of them is the abort clause absent**, because `failureKind` can only be non-null with zero missing ids via the `anyAborted` branch. The one shape that could read as "failed but nothing is missing" always ships its own explanation in the same string.

The operator-facing message also had **no content assertion anywhere** — only `toBeTruthy()`. This commit rewrote the artifact of the whole mechanism with nothing pinning its shape; content assertions were added and proven non-vacuous by reverting `formatMissingIds` and observing the exact expected failure.

## Verification worth recording

All three TASK-199 mutation plants were re-run independently by the reviewer with counts matching the developer's exactly, including **Plant B** (`shippedPinWins` dropped → the deferred-not-planned test fails) — the one guarding the deferred-replace exclusion, where a regression would make a correct keep-as-is run report `ok: false`. Over-correction was also chased **structurally**, not just by cases: for a planned install id to be absent from the landed set while the op succeeded, the skill would have to become live by something other than an install op, and `src/pack-reconcile.js:207` makes install the only materializer — so that false alarm is unreachable.

**Concurrency handling, noted approvingly.** Hitting 2 failures from another agent's live edits, the developer stashed only the unrelated dirty paths, verified its bundle byte-matched a clean-tree build, then stash-popped to restore the other agent's work — rather than committing dist from a contaminated tree or chasing another ticket's red. It then reported plainly that its run was not a clean green and why. **I re-ran `test:all` myself once the tree quiesced: 191 passed | 1 skipped (192 files), 2222 passed | 4 skipped, 0 failed** — confirming the attribution.

## Findings accepted without rework

- **MEDIUM (process)** — the pre-hand-off checklist stated outcomes for only two of five items in the reviewer's inputs. **DISCHARGED:** the raw hand-off carried all five, and the reviewer independently verified the three unstated ones clean (parity genuinely n/a — `commands/` has no `.claude/` copy).
- **Carry-forward, not a blocker:** identical non-string planned ids collapse to one `Set` entry, so `missingInstallIds` under-counts malformed ops while `ok` stays correctly `false` — it under-counts the diagnostic, never under-reports the failure. Same `Set`-collapse the JSDoc already documents for duplicate ids.
- **Declined:** the minimalism nit on `plannedIdentityTotal`/`matchedIdentityTotal` being scalars reconstructed from the Sets. Preserving the old three-branch expression shape aids reviewability against the prior version.

`dist/pack-ctl.cjs` is byte-fresh; the `47961c8` delta is 9 insertions / 5 deletions across four hunks, each mapping 1:1 to a source change. Confirmed TASK-207's later rebuild of the same bundle did not clobber it.
